exchanges.channelBindingEncoding: Four-byte big-endian length plus exact verified Access-Request; four-byte big-endian length plus EAP session ID from the verified Access-Accept. This is an evidence encoding of the authenticated backend exchange, not a TLS exporter or a claim of RFC 6677 channel binding.
exchanges.implementationBoundary: OpenSSL verifies handshake signatures and Finished; hostap verifies RADIUS integrity and decrypts protected key attributes. Public records and opaque key hashes bind those observed operations. The parser does not independently verify secret-dependent cryptography.
exchanges.transcriptEncoding: Concatenated TLS 1.3 Handshake structures, including their one-byte type and three-byte length, through client Finished. CompressedCertificate bytes are retained as sent.

scope: A successful TLS exchange between the supplicant and AS; authenticator receives the MSK through RADIUS.
The authenticator has no separate client TLS handshake or client certificate in this exchange.
Equal SHA-256 references bind observations under the collector and collision-resistance assumptions; secret values are not exported.
MACsec headers bind SCI and association number after installation. Payload probes cover selected packets, not every possible execution.
Instrumentation and Linux/OpenSSL behavior remain implementation assumptions; no product certification or universal protocol-conformance claim.
Exact public initial TLS transcript, hello randoms, EAP session, verified backend records and full-MSK hashes are bound to the captured exchange.

Causal links come from same-process event order and matching public MKA messages. No physical total order across processes is inferred. Hostap's successful integrity checks remain implementation observations.

AS completion reaches both CAK derivations through same-process order and exact RADIUS/EAP-Success messages. Timestamps remain capture sanity checks and do not generate causal links. Hostap/OpenSSL verification and instrumentation remain implementation observations.
